item.title: Safe AI pathfinding is essential for government adoption, officials say
item.description: GSA's architecture lead for AI services said standardized evaluation helps users identify the right models for their needs.

item.title: The Pentagon’s ‘woke AI’ problem
item.description: Commentary | From a political bias perspective, eliminating Claude from the federal toolkit removes a model that has made significant strides toward the neutrality ideal pushed by the administration.

item.title: CMS seeks to expand tech-driven fight against Medicaid fraud
item.description: The agency is looking at “testing new approaches and really being able to think outside of the box” to claw back improper payments, according to CMS COO Kim Brandt.

item.title: White House releases regulatory vision for AI
item.description: The framework includes seven AI policy recommendations for Congress that attempt to balance consumer protections with advancing AI development.

item.title: New methods for assuring digital identity and authenticity
item.description: COMMENTARY | Authenticity and provenance must be enforced both at the application level and at the system level so agencies can be confident that user identity and the identity mechanisms themselves are genuine and trustworthy.

item.title: Tech bills of the week: Anti-AI moratorium efforts; Supporting small AI businesses; and more
item.description: Lawmakers rolled out a number of proposals this week focused on deploying or reviewing uses of AI, including legislation to leverage the tech in the energy grid and democratize the industry landscape.

item.title: Lawmaker calls for GAO review of threat actors weaponizing AI
item.description: In a letter to the federal watchdog, Rep. August Pfluger, R-Texas, warned that “the nature and scope of the challenges associated with countering these AI-enabled threats are not well understood.”

item.title: ‘No practical use': TSA experts say Trump’s ICE deployments won’t help with airport security
item.description: More than 400 TSA employees have left the agency since the shutdown began last month, White House says.

item.title: Google launches threat disruption unit, stops short of calling it ‘offensive’
item.description: The unit will use legal authorizations and technical capabilities to impede cyber threat groups, though company execs say it will not go so far as to hack into adversaries' systems.

item.title: Mullin confirmed to lead DHS as shutdown drags on and 100,000 employees remain unpaid
item.description: Trump's new DHS chief promises some reforms and renewed staffing efforts.
